messages:
jun: heads up — we just started seeing a big spike in pod evictions in ap-southeast2 since ~12:03 UTC. eviction_rate ~12/min, mostly ML training pods. root reason in events is `NodeAffinity`/`preemption` after the rack-label rollout. any ideas? :eyes:

sre-bot: ALERT ap-southeast2: eviction_rate=12/min (5m avg) · affected=~220 pods · nodesNotReady=3 · time=2025-10-11T12:04:02Z

nate: ugh. was the new rack label applied cluster-wide? last I saw it was gated but maybe rollout hit ap-southeast2 early. which label key?

jun: label is `rack=fast-3` -> applied to nodes in a few pools as part of rack-aware placement experiment. rollout PR: https://git.internal/rack-label-rollout/PR-472. we intended it for canary only but looks like 3 ASGs got the label.

ida: quick ask — can you paste a sample pod event? want to confirm eviction reason looks like affinity mismatch vs OOM.

jun: pasted sample event: ```
Warning  FailedScheduling  2s (x7 over 12s)  default-scheduler  0/18 nodes are available: 9 node(s) had taint {rack=fast-3:NoSchedule}, tolerations not found, 6 node(s) didn't match node affinity, 3 node(s) were NotReady.
Warning  Evicted  1s (x3 over 10s)  kubelet  The node was low on resource: ephemeral-storage.```

maria: two things: (1) the rollout added a taint + label combo? that explains tolerations missing. (2) ephemeral-storage eviction line worries me — could be unrelated co-occurrence (logs show nodes with disk pressure too).

nate: if it's taint+label from the rollout then adding tolerations to deployments is a short-term fix, but we shouldn't patch hundreds of deploys. rollback label rollout ASAP.

ida: agree. also check kubelet heartbeat/network. nodesNotReady=3 in alert — I saw earlier a control-plane egress blip to ap-southeast2 which caused kubelets to spike in reconnects. when a node goes NotReady the scheduler may preempt and then affinity changes keep pods oscillating.

ops: i'm starting emergency actions: 1) pausing the rack-label rollout, 2) scaling warm pool in ap-southeast2 by +20 GPUs (warm pool -> dedicated warm nodes) to reduce pending/thrashing, 3) hold new deployments in that region. estimated incremental cost ~+$6k/hr if we keep the extra warm pool for an hour.

jun: please pause rollout +1. ops can you also mark the three NotReady nodes as unschedulable so we don't keep trying to place there?

ops: marking nodes cordoned and draining non-critical jobs now. running: `kubectl cordon node-apse2-12 && kubectl drain node-apse2-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data`

maria: we should push a hotfix to the rollout job to only apply the label to the canary ASG and remove the taint part. looks like the automation accidentally toggled both label and taint. PR in flight: https://git.internal/rack-label-rollout/PR-478 (revert taint + re-narrow targets)

nate: another mitigation: scheduler config has topologySpread weights that prefer rack-local placement which, combined with sudden label changes, amplifies fragmentation. can we temporarily relax the topology weight so the scheduler is less strict for 30m?

ida: bumping that could reduce churn. config is in configmap `kube-scheduler-config` in kube-system. a quick `kubectl -n kube-system edit configmap kube-scheduler-config` to set `topologySpreadConstraints` weight lower should be fine as short-term. thanks @nate for catching that.

jun: i pulled kube-scheduler logs, here's an excerpt showing scheduling failures: ```
I1011 12:05:12.123456 1 scheduler.go:234] predicate failed: NodeAffinity: node(s) didn't match node affinity; failedPods=180
I1011 12:05:20.789012 1 binder.go:198] preempting 3 pods to make room for high-priority batch-job-xyz
I1011 12:06:01.345678 1 schedule_attempt.go:67] backoff for pod=ml-train-foo: 30s
```

ops: warm pool scaled +20 GPUs (added 5 nodes) in ap-southeast2, will keep for 30m and monitor. cost impact noted in #finance.

maria: i'm merging the rollback PR to remove taint and constrain rollout. should be live in ~3m.

nate: i'm going to lower topology weight to 1 (from 10) for the next 45 minutes. will revert after.

ida: observed control-plane egress errors in cloud provider logs correlated with the first NotReady events. sending ticket to cloud-networking to check route table flaps — but this isn't purely a scheduler bug. still, our rollout/automation made the system brittle.

jun: plan of action agreed: 1) pause label/taint rollout (done), 2) remove the accidental taint (in progress by maria), 3) relax topology weights (nate), 4) scale warm pool + cordon NotReady nodes (ops), 5) open postmortem and add a rollout safety gate. i'll write the incident doc after we stabilize.

ops: current numbers 12:12 UTC: eviction_rate down to 3/min, pending pods dropping from 420 -> 140. will update in 10m. :thumbsup:

maria: merging completed. tag `rack-rollout@reverted-taint` created.

nate: topology weight reverted back to original at 12:38 UTC.

ida: cloud-team confirmed a transient route table update from 12:01-12:06 which caused kubelet reconnects. they also suggested we add a kubelet backoff tweak to avoid immediate eviction cascade in future. filing follow-up.

jun: thanks all. assigning postmortem ownership to me, will include cost analysis on warm pool bump and propose a safer rollout pattern (canary + automated smoke jobs + guardrail to prevent taints without tolerations). :pray:
